newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 10.

text.p: There are 82 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that banning foreign donations to local political parties, as suggested by Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office, should include those from China and Taiwan. China could remain unchanged by criticism from foreign countries, but it would be a deadly blow if Hong Kong lost its good reputation internationally. The paper urged the post-handover government to be careful passing laws which restrict the right to hold demonstrations and other rights.

-- The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said the proposed plan by Tung's office to restrict demonstrations and ban overseas donations to local political parties was a good balance between public interest and individual rights. The paper said that after consulting Hong Kong people, the proposal should be able to be passed smoothly by the provisional legislative council before the handover.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that Hnng Kong had been remarkably peaceful and law abiding, and a wide degree of tolerance went hand-in-hand with general respect for the boundaries of civil liberties. The paper said that it was time for serious debate during the consultation period for the proposal to change two human rights ordinances. The fact that the changes were felt to be so important by the future authorities could only be seen as a sign of a more restrictive approach which placed insufficient faith in the civic sense of the people of the territory.
